environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed on EC2 with a custom AppArmor profile loaded as 'report-service-confined'. The profile is set to enforce mode and uses a deny-by-default posture with explicit path allowances. The profile permits read access to /opt/app/templates/**, write access to /opt/app/output/**, execute access ONLY to /opt/app/bin/report-engine and /usr/bin/node, and denies all network raw/packet capabilities. Critically, the profile includes 'deny /etc/shadow r,' 'deny /proc/*/environ r,' 'deny /**/sh ix,' 'deny /**/bash ix,' 'deny /**/dash ix,' and 'deny capability sys_ptrace'. The ix (inherit execute) denial on shell interpreters means that even though exec() is called, the kernel refuses to execute /bin/sh which child_process.exec() requires as its shell. The profile was generated via aa-genprof during normal operation and then hardened with explicit deny rules for shell access patterns.
